TOLLAMERE, 14 March 2031 (Meridian Brief) — Lithium brine has been found at the Hadrow Flats survey site, according to preliminary assay results released Friday.

Brine samples drawn from 18 test wells averaged 412 milligrams of lithium per litre, the Hadrow Flats Preliminary Assay Report (Report No. HFS-31-07) shows. The document was presented at a public briefing held by the Hadrow Flats Survey Consortium in Tollamere.

Dr. Perrin Valkoski, the Consortium's lead field geochemist, oversaw the sampling program, people familiar with the matter said.

Those people said the results confirm the presence of lithium-bearing brine across the tested area. They cautioned that the figures are preliminary and that further assay work would be needed before any assessment of the deposit's wider extent.

The Consortium has not announced a timetable for additional testing.

Meridian Brief will update this item as further details emerge.
